structure: Part 1 read the whole ruling file ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates.md (78 lines): three verbatim quotes from Sam (point 8 on the INS front door, point 8a on what 'the dashboard' means and on templates, point 7b on plants), a framing paragraph (templates theme split off for a second machine; claims marked 'applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle' are not Sam's words; plants evidence is plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json), then seven numbered claims under '(a) The dashboard' (claims 1-3) and '(b) Templates' (claims 4-7), with sub-bullets under claims 4, 6 and 7 and an orchestrator note under claim 6. Every numbered claim and sub-bullet was checked against the verbatim quotes: what the quotes say in so many words is verbatim, the main session's readings and the orchestrator's applications are inferred and say so. Gaps record what the ruling touches and leaves open: the template-mode validation difference, when the dashboard requirements firm up, the detail of the animals dashboard restyle, and what 'Use template' does beyond going ahead.

claims.statement: The templates theme is split off from the backlog and built separately (on a second machine) while the rest of the backlog is still being ruled on.
claims.quote: Sam wants the templates theme split off and built on a second machine while the rest of the backlog is still being ruled on. This ruling covers only what that needs.
claims.note: Written by the main session, not a quote from Sam. It also states that claims marked 'applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle' are the orchestrator's calls, not Sam's words; claims 3 (plants part), 6 (transporter note) and 7 are such calls.

claims.statement: The INS dashboard's summary information is blocked: no changes are made to it in this programme.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates.md point 8 and point 8a quotes; claim 1
claims.quote: the dashboard stuff is really early. The INS dashboard requirements are still really early days. That stuff's blocked. We can't be making changes.
claims.note: Answers point 8 and 8a of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md. Point 8a narrows 'the dashboard' to the summary information: 'I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit.'

claims.statement: The blocked INS dashboard summary information includes the count of notifications.
claims.quote: The dashboard, as in the summary information that you have this many notifications or this many status changes. That's all massive stuff. Has not been sort of bounced off anyone.
claims.note: Answers point 8a of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md.

claims.statement: The blocked INS dashboard summary information includes the status-change cards (how many status changes there have been).
claims.quote: this many status changes. That's all massive stuff.
claims.note: 'Cards' is the main session's word in claim 1; the quote says 'this many status changes'.

claims.statement: The drill-downs from the INS dashboard summary information are blocked too.
claims.quote: INS front door: overall dashboard, drill-downs and the notification lists. Here, the dashboard stuff is really early. ... That stuff's blocked.
claims.note: Answers point 8 of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md.

claims.statement: Backlog rows for the INS dashboard summary information stay in the backlog, marked blocked, rather than being removed; it follows from Sam calling them blocked rather than out of scope.
claims.quote: That stuff's blocked.
claims.note: Claim 1 reads: 'Those rows stay in the backlog, blocked'. The main session's reading of 'blocked'.

claims.statement: The INS dashboard summary area is re-distilled once its requirements exist; it follows from Sam saying the requirements are still early and have not been agreed with anyone.
claims.quote: The INS dashboard requirements are still really early days. ... Has not been sort of bounced off anyone.
claims.note: Claim 1: 'the area is re-distilled once requirements exist'.

claims.statement: Nothing on the INS home page other than the summary information is blocked: buttons on the home page are explicitly outside the block.
claims.quote: I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit. Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: Answers point 8a of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md.

claims.statement: The INS home page's 'Create new' button goes ahead; it follows from Sam saying the block covers only the summary information, not the buttons.
claims.quote: I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit. Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: The quote names only 'a button on there to create a template'; the 'Create new' button label is the main session's reading in claim 2.

claims.statement: The INS home page's 'Use template' button goes ahead; it follows from Sam excluding the template button from the dashboard block.
claims.quote: Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: Sam's words say 'create a template'; claim 2 names the button 'Use template'. The exact label and which button(s) are the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The 'What are you importing?' question, asked before a notification is created, goes ahead; it follows from Sam limiting the block to the summary information and calling template creation simple CRUD.
claims.quote: I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit. Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: Not named in any quote; the main session lists it in claims 2 and 4. Copy: 'What are you importing?'.

claims.statement: The Templates navigation item goes ahead; it follows from templates being CRUD work that is not blocked.
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud. That's simple.
claims.note: Not named in any quote; the main session lists it in claims 2 and 4.

claims.statement: A backlog row that depends on the INS home page depends only on its 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons, the type question and the Templates navigation item existing, not on the summary information; it follows from the block covering only the summary information.
claims.quote: I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit. Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: Dependency rule for the backlog, the main session's reading.

claims.statement: A separate theme changes the animals frontend's own dashboard so it looks more like the animals dashboard in the prototype.
claims.quote: Something we could potentially do, maybe as a separate theme, is changes to the animals dashboard, so the animals dashboard looks more like the animals dashboard on the prototype. That'd be good.
claims.note: Answers point 8 of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md. Sam's words are tentative ('could potentially', 'maybe'); claim 3 states it as a new theme.

claims.statement: The live animals notification list stays in the animals frontend and is not moved to the INS frontend in this programme; it follows from Sam directing changes at the animals dashboard while blocking the INS dashboard.
claims.quote: INS front door: overall dashboard, drill-downs and the notification lists. ... That stuff's blocked. We can't be making changes. Something we could potentially do, maybe as a separate theme, is changes to the animals dashboard
claims.note: Claim 3 says this replaces, for this programme, the move of the list to the INS frontend that claim 22 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 kept from DR1.

claims.statement: Plants' own notification list is reframed in the same increments as the animals dashboard restyle; the orchestrator applied this from Sam's principle that plants and animals get a common change at the same time.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call, not Sam's ruling. Cites plants-common-mapping and point 7c.

claims.statement: Templates are create, read, update and delete work and go ahead now, not blocked with the dashboard.
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud. That's simple.
claims.note: Answers point 8a of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md.

claims.statement: There is a Manage templates page, in the templates work that goes ahead; it follows from templates being CRUD.
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud.
claims.note: The main session's listing; not named in the quote.

claims.statement: A user can start a template; Sam names creating a template as CRUD that goes ahead.
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud. That's simple.

claims.statement: A user can save a template; it follows from templates being CRUD (create and update).
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud.

claims.statement: A user can view a template; it follows from templates being CRUD (read).
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud.

claims.statement: A user can change a template; it follows from templates being CRUD (update).
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud.

claims.statement: A user can use a template to start a notification; it follows from Sam excluding the template button on the home page from the block.
claims.quote: Not a button on there to create a template. ... "Create a template" is fucking crud.

claims.statement: A user can discard a template they have started; it follows from templates being CRUD.
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud.

claims.statement: A user can delete a template; it follows from templates being CRUD (delete).
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud.

claims.statement: Template mode is another way of walking through the same journey pages as a notification.
claims.quote: this needs to be another way of walking through the same pages
claims.note: Answers point 8a of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md.

claims.statement: Template mode captures the same data as the notification journey.
claims.quote: maybe capturing the same data with different validation. I don't know
claims.note: Sam hedges ('maybe', 'I don't know').

claims.statement: Template mode may apply different validation from the notification journey on the same pages.
claims.quote: maybe capturing the same data with different validation. I don't know
claims.note: Tentative; see the gap on which validation differs.

claims.statement: Template mode is built so that later changes to the journey pages carry into template mode without rework.
claims.quote: There are going to be changes again in the future. You can't be fucking implementing something in such a way that it can't handle journey changes.

claims.statement: Template mode must not copy pages or fork the journey for templates; it follows from Sam requiring the same pages and resilience to journey changes.
claims.quote: this needs to be another way of walking through the same pages

claims.statement: Template rows do not wait for other themes' changes to the pages they walk through; they work on the pages as they stand when built, and later page changes carry over. It follows from Sam rejecting finishing development before building.
claims.quote: you can't fucking go, "Right, we're just going to finish development forever, and then we'll take a coffee."

claims.statement: A template row keeps a dependency on another theme's row only where it needs something that row creates and that does not exist today, such as a page, a field or a stored value.
claims.quote: You can't be fucking implementing something in such a way that it can't handle journey changes.
claims.note: The main session's dependency rule derived from claim 5's principle.

claims.statement: A template row's dependency that exists only because a page's look or order will change is dropped; examples are the overview's new regions, the review's new headings and the reordered opening run.
claims.quote: There are going to be changes again in the future. You can't be fucking implementing something in such a way that it can't handle journey changes.
claims.note: The examples are the main session's, not Sam's.

claims.statement: In template mode, the transporter list's buttons follow today's transporter list; the orchestrator applied this from Sam's principle that template mode works on pages as they stand.
claims.quote: Applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle: the transporter list's buttons in template mode follow today's transporter list.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call, not Sam's ruling.

claims.statement: Transporter management is blocked separately, not by this ruling.
claims.quote: Transporter management is blocked separately (answers point 5).
claims.note: The main session's statement, referring to point 5 of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md; no Sam quote in this ruling supports it.

claims.statement: A change that applies to both plants and animals is made to both in the same increment, not in a separate plants increment.
claims.quote: it's massive overkill to double the number of increments to see if there's an [plants] equivalent. ... [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time. The overhead of adding an increment is relatively expensive, so we don't want to be needlessly separating things.
claims.note: Answers point 7b of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md.

claims.statement: Common pages and behaviour between plants and animals are identified by a workflow, to find where a plants change is required.
claims.quote: A workflow: go through and identify common pages, common behaviour, and where it's required.
claims.note: The framing paragraph names the resulting evidence: plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json.

claims.statement: Where a templates row changes something plants also has, the same increment changes plants; the orchestrator applied this from Sam's point 7b principle.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call, not Sam's ruling.

claims.statement: Starting from the INS 'What are you importing?' type question gives plants the same entry: choosing plants creates a plants draft and lands on plants' first page.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's application of point 7b.

claims.statement: The Templates navigation item is added to plants' navigation too, linking across to Manage templates.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's application of point 7b. 'Linking across' implies Manage templates lives outside the plants frontend.

claims.statement: Back links follow the context a page was opened in (such as template mode or a notification), in animals and in plants.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's application of point 7b; the context-following back link itself is stated by the main session, not quoted from Sam.

claims.statement: In plants, context-following back links use plants' own step order.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's application of point 7b.

claims.statement: Back from the first page of the journey to the INS type question is animals only, because plants' first page is its own type question.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call: an exception to point 7b where plants does not share the page.

claims.statement: Template mode on journey pages is animals only: plants pages get no template mode, because templates cover the animals sets.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call: the stated reason is 'templates cover the animals sets'; no Sam quote says templates are animals only.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say which validation differs in template mode from the notification journey (for example whether mandatory fields may be left blank in a template).
claims.note: Sam: 'maybe capturing the same data with different validation. I don't know'. Claim 5: 'perhaps with different validation'.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say when or by whom the INS dashboard requirements will firm up, so it leaves open when the blocked rows are re-distilled.

The ruling does not say which parts of the prototype's animals dashboard the animals frontend's dashboard should take on, or whether the restyle theme is definitely in scope (Sam says 'could potentially', 'maybe').

The ruling does not say what 'Use template' does when a user chooses a template (for example whether it copies the template into a new draft notification or opens it), nor where Manage templates lives (INS frontend or animals frontend).
